question:
A 29-year-old female presents for evaluation following a positive home pregnancy test. She reports
nausea with multiple episodes of vomiting and increased urinary frequency over the past week. Her
sexual history includes inconsistent condom use with her boyfriend, and her last menstrual period was
5 weeks ago. Physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory testing confirms pregnancy and HPV
positivity. A Pap smear reveals a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, while colposcopy with
cervical biopsy demonstrates cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grades II and III. What is the most
appropriate next step in managing this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Antiviral therapy for HPV
suppression (B) Immediate cryotherapy of the cervical lesion (C) Colposcopy and HPV-based testing in
12 weeks (D) Weekly colposcopy throughout pregnancy (E) Cold-knife conization 4 weeks after birth
(F) Expedited treatment with loop electrosurgical excision (G) HPV vaccination series initiation (H)
Laser ablation after first trimester (I) Cervical cytology every 4 weeks during pregnancy (J) Postpone all
interventions until after delivery
 A. Expedited treatment with loop electrosurgical excision
B. Laser ablation after first trimester
C. HPV vaccination series initiation
D. Weekly colposcopy throughout pregnancy
E. Cervical cytology every 4 weeks during pregnancy
F. Cold-knife conization 4 weeks after birth
G. Colposcopy and HPV-based testing in 12 weeks
H. Immediate cryotherapy of the cervical lesion
I. Postpone all interventions until after delivery
J. Antiviral therapy for HPV suppression
